explanation: Carry the allowed inclusive value range down the tree. A left child inherits an upper bound at its parent’s value; a right child inherits a lower bound there. Inclusive bounds preserve this corpus’s rule that duplicate keys may occur on either side.
timeComplexity: O(n) time. Each node contributes one range check and each pending branch lies along a traversal path.
spaceComplexity: O(h) auxiliary stack space for height h. Traversal frames hold a node and two bounds along pending branches.
attribution: JavaScript port of the independently authored EPI Practice C# algorithm; no upstream reference code copied.
correctness: Each stack entry records exactly the inclusive range imposed by that node’s ancestors. Checking the value and propagating tighter bounds to its children enforces every ancestor constraint, not merely parent-child comparisons. Inclusive endpoints implement the EPI rule allowing equal keys on either side.
walkthrough: For level order [6,6,9,null,null,8,9], the left 6 satisfies the upper bound 6. The right 9 and its children 8 and 9 lie within their inclusive ancestor ranges. Return true. The walkthroughCase uses the judge’s JSON input format and expected observation.
edgeCases: Duplicate values are permitted by this EPI contract.
A descendant can violate a distant ancestor even if it is correctly ordered relative to its parent.
Long bounds include int.MinValue and int.MaxValue safely.
